subject: chemistry
name: Chemistry

pillars.name: Concepts
pillars.scope: The student holds a wrong idea about matter, particles, bonding, reactions or energy.

pillars.name: Strategy & Setup
pillars.scope: The ideas are sound, but the plan is wrong: the wrong relationship, reaction, ratio or experimental design.

pillars.name: Procedure
pillars.scope: The plan is right, but carrying out the method goes wrong (stoichiometry steps, naming, formulas, Lewis structures, equilibrium expressions).

pillars.name: Calculation & Recall
pillars.scope: Method and plan are sound; a number, molar mass, constant, charge, unit or rounding slips.

pillars.name: Communication
pillars.scope: The chemistry may be right, but the answer is not what was asked, is written in wrong notation, or is not explained.

pillars.name: Test Habits
pillars.scope: How the student handles the test: blanks, traps, giving up, not checking, not using the data sheet.

decision_order: Is the student's idea of the chemistry wrong (CON)?
Is the idea right but the relationship, reaction, mole ratio or design wrong (STR)?
Is the plan right but a step of the method done wrongly (PRC)?
Is it a slip in a number, molar mass, constant, charge, unit or rounding (FAC)?
Is the chemistry right but the answer not what was asked, in wrong notation, or unexplained (COM)?
Or is it how the test was handled (TST)?

codes.name: Bulk Properties Given to Particles
codes.plain_name: Gave particles properties they don't have
codes.student_help: Single particles don't melt, expand or change colour; only the spaces and motions between them change.
codes.description: Gives individual atoms or molecules the visible properties of the substance (molecules expand when heated, copper atoms are orange, particles melt).
codes.example: 'When the gas is heated, the molecules get bigger, so the balloon expands.'

tell_apart.how: If the error is about which bonds break during a change of state, use CON_INTER_INTRA_FORCES.
If the student means the right thing and only words it loosely ('the particles spread out' for the gas), use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: particle diagram before and after the change.

codes.name: Intermolecular vs Intramolecular Forces
codes.plain_name: Mixed up forces between and within molecules
codes.student_help: Boiling and melting separate molecules from each other; the bonds inside each molecule stay.
codes.description: Confuses forces between molecules with bonds inside them (boiling water breaks O-H bonds; a stronger covalent bond means a higher boiling point).
codes.example: 'When water boils, the bonds between hydrogen and oxygen break, so the bubbles are hydrogen and oxygen gas.'

tell_apart.how: CON_PARTICLE_PROPERTIES is about giving particles bulk properties; this code is about which forces a change affects.
If the error is about whether bond breaking takes in or gives out energy, use CON_BOND_ENERGY.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: two-level diagram of molecules with bonds inside and attractions between.

codes.name: Bond Breaking Releases Energy
codes.plain_name: Thinks breaking bonds gives out energy
codes.student_help: Breaking bonds always takes energy in; making bonds gives energy out.
codes.description: Believes breaking bonds releases energy, or that energy is stored 'in' a bond and let out when it breaks; gets the sign of ΔH backwards as a result.
codes.example: 'ATP releases energy because its phosphate bond breaks.' / 'Combustion is exothermic because the fuel's bonds break.'

tell_apart.how: If the student knows which way energy flows but writes ΔH with the wrong sign or on the wrong side, use PRC_ENERGY_SIGN.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: energy-level diagram with bond breaking and bond making drawn as separate steps.

codes.name: Mass Not Conserved
codes.plain_name: Thinks mass is lost or gained in reactions
codes.student_help: Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed; a gas that escapes still has mass.
codes.description: Believes mass disappears when a gas is produced or appears when a solid forms, or that a reaction can make or destroy atoms.
codes.example: 'The mass went down after burning the steel wool... wait, it went up, so mass was created.'

tell_apart.how: If the student accepts conservation but balances incorrectly, use PRC_BALANCING.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: closed-system demonstration and atom counting.

codes.name: Ionic Compounds as Molecules
codes.plain_name: Treated an ionic compound like a molecule
codes.student_help: Ionic compounds are lattices of ions; there is no single 'NaCl molecule' and electrons are transferred, not shared.
codes.description: Treats ionic compounds as discrete molecules, describes ionic bonding as sharing, or draws a single bond between a metal and non-metal ion.
codes.example: 'One molecule of NaCl has a covalent bond where Na and Cl share an electron.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea of ions is right but the formula is built wrongly from the charges, use PRC_FORMULA_FROM_IONS.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: lattice model next to a molecular model.

codes.name: What a Mole Means
codes.plain_name: Mixed up what a mole counts
codes.student_help: A mole is a count of particles; check whether you are counting molecules or the atoms inside them.
codes.description: Treats the mole as a mass, or confuses moles of a compound with moles of the atoms in it (1 mol O₂ contains 1 mol O atoms).
codes.example: '1 mol of O₂ has a mass of 16 g, the same as 1 mol of O.'

tell_apart.how: If the student understands the mole and just adds the periodic table masses wrongly, use FAC_MOLAR_MASS.
If the mole idea is right and the ratio from the equation is wrong, use STR_WRONG_MOLE_RATIO.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: counting analogy (a dozen eggs vs a dozen cartons).

codes.name: Equilibrium as Stopped
codes.plain_name: Thinks equilibrium means the reaction stops
codes.student_help: At equilibrium both reactions still happen at the same rate; amounts stay constant, not equal.
codes.description: Believes reactions stop at equilibrium, that concentrations of reactants and products are equal, or that Le Châtelier shifts change K when only concentration changes.
codes.example: 'At equilibrium the reaction is finished, so [N₂] = [NH₃].'

tell_apart.how: If the idea is right but the K expression or ICE table is built wrongly, use PRC_EQUILIBRIUM_EXPRESSION.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: two-way traffic simulation with equal rates.

codes.name: Strong vs Concentrated
codes.student_help: Strong means it ionises completely; concentrated means there is a lot of it per litre.
codes.description: Confuses acid or base strength (degree of ionisation) with concentration, or thinks a weak acid cannot have a low pH.
codes.example: '0.001 mol/L HCl is a weak acid because it is dilute.'

tell_apart.how: If the student understands strength and just misremembers which acids are strong, use FAC_SCIENCE_FACT_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: particle pictures of strong/weak × dilute/concentrated grid.

codes.name: Formula / Law Misselection
codes.student_help: The formula or rule used here does not fit this type of question.
codes.description: Applies a formula, theorem or law whose conditions the problem does not meet.
codes.example: Uses Boyle's law (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂) on a question where the temperature also changes, instead of the combined gas law.

tell_apart.how: Here the formula itself is wrong for the situation; in STR_WRONG_SUBSTITUTION the formula is right but the givens go into the wrong places.

codes.remediation: Condition check table: list each formula with the conditions it needs, then tick which ones the question meets.

codes.name: Unbalanced Equation Used
codes.student_help: Balance the equation before you take any mole ratio from it.
codes.description: Takes mole ratios or mass predictions from an equation that has not been balanced.
codes.example: Uses H₂ + O₂ → H₂O as written and concludes 1 mol H₂ gives 1 mol H₂O from 1 mol O₂.

tell_apart.how: If the student tried to balance and got it wrong, use PRC_BALANCING; this code is for not balancing at all.
If the equation is balanced and the ratio is read wrongly, use STR_WRONG_MOLE_RATIO.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: 'balance before you ratio' checkpoint.

codes.name: Wrong Mole Ratio
codes.student_help: Write the ratio as (wanted coefficient / given coefficient) with the names next to the numbers.
codes.description: Uses a balanced equation but inverts the mole ratio, takes the coefficient of the wrong species, or skips the ratio (assumes 1:1).
codes.example: For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, finds mol O₂ needed for 4 mol H₂ as 4 × 2/1 = 8 mol.

tell_apart.how: If the equation was never balanced, use STR_UNBALANCED_EQUATION_USED.
If the student does not understand what the coefficients count, use CON_MOLE_MEANING.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: labelled ratio bridge (mol wanted / mol given).

codes.name: Limiting Reagent Ignored
codes.student_help: When amounts of two reactants are given, work out which one runs out first.
codes.description: When amounts of more than one reactant are given, calculates the product from the excess reactant or from both added together.
codes.example: Given 2.0 mol H₂ and 2.0 mol O₂, predicts 4.0 mol H₂O from the oxygen.

tell_apart.how: If the limiting reactant is chosen correctly but the ratio is wrong, use STR_WRONG_MOLE_RATIO.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: 'which runs out first' table for each reactant.

codes.name: Wrong Reaction Predicted
codes.plain_name: Predicted the wrong reaction or products
codes.student_help: Classify the reaction type first, then check the activity series or solubility table.
codes.description: Predicts the wrong reaction type or products: a displacement the activity series rules out, a precipitate that is soluble, the wrong products of combustion or neutralisation.
codes.example: Predicts Cu + ZnSO₄ → CuSO₄ + Zn even though copper is below zinc in the activity series.

tell_apart.how: If the products are right but their formulas are written wrongly, use PRC_FORMULA_FROM_IONS.
If the activity series or solubility table was provided and ignored, use TST_REFERENCE_SHEET_UNUSED.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: reaction-type decision tree.

codes.name: Wrong Substitution
codes.plain_name: Values put in the wrong places
codes.student_help: The right formula was used, but values went into the wrong spots.
codes.description: Puts known values into the wrong variables of a correct formula.
codes.example: In C₁V₁ = C₂V₂, puts the volume of water added in as V₂ instead of the total final volume.

tell_apart.how: If the formula is wrong for the situation, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION; this code is only for the right formula filled in wrongly.
If the student read the number itself wrongly from the question, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN; here the number is read right but given the wrong role.

codes.remediation: Givens list: symbol, value, unit for every quantity before any substitution.

codes.name: No Viable Plan
codes.student_help: The first move here could not lead to the answer. Plan the method before writing.
codes.description: Starts with a move that cannot reach the answer, or moves symbols around with no method.
codes.example: Asked for the mass of product from a mass of reactant, writes n = m/M and PV = nRT with no route between the two substances.

tell_apart.how: STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION is one wrong choice inside a sensible plan; this code is for when no workable plan is visible at all.
If there is only an answer with no work, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS; this code needs visible work that wanders.

codes.remediation: Plan-first prompt: name the target, the known quantities and the bridge between them before calculating.

codes.name: Experimental Design Flaw
codes.student_help: Change one thing, measure one thing, and keep everything else the same.
codes.description: Gets the independent, dependent or controlled variables wrong, leaves out a control or repeats, or designs a test that cannot answer the question.
codes.example: Tests how temperature affects reaction rate but also changes the acid concentration between trials.

tell_apart.how: This code is about how the experiment is set up; COM_OBSERVATION_VS_INFERENCE is about how the results are reported.
STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN is for calculation problems; use this code for planning an investigation.

codes.remediation: Fair-test frame: I will change ___, measure ___, and keep ___ the same; repeat ___ times.

codes.name: Step Omission
codes.student_help: A needed step in the method was skipped.
codes.description: Skips a required step of the procedure, so the result does not follow.
codes.example: Applies the mole ratio directly to grams (mass of reactant × 2/1) without converting to moles first.

tell_apart.how: Here a middle step is missing and the answer is wrong; in PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION the work is right but stops before the end.
If the plan itself is missing, use STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN; here the plan is right and one step drops out.

codes.remediation: Faded worked example: complete the one missing step in an otherwise finished solution.

codes.name: Balancing Method Error
codes.student_help: Only change the big numbers in front; never change the small subscripts.
codes.description: Tries to balance but changes subscripts instead of coefficients, or leaves atoms unbalanced (often oxygen or polyatomic ions).
codes.example: Balances H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by writing H₂ + O₂ → H₂O₂.

tell_apart.how: If no balancing was attempted, use STR_UNBALANCED_EQUATION_USED.
If the student doesn't accept that atoms are conserved, use CON_MASS_CONSERVATION.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: atom-count table under each side of the equation.

codes.name: Formula from Ions
codes.plain_name: Built the formula wrongly from the ions
codes.student_help: Make the total positive and negative charges equal; use brackets for more than one polyatomic ion.
codes.description: Builds a formula whose charges don't balance, forgets brackets around polyatomic ions, or crosses charges without reducing.
codes.example: Writes calcium nitrate as CaNO₃₂ or Ca₂(NO₃).

tell_apart.how: If the student uses the wrong charge for an ion, use FAC_ION_CHARGE_RECALL; this code is for a wrong formula from the right charges.
If the student does not see the compound as ionic at all, use CON_IONIC_AS_MOLECULE.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: charge-box method for each ion.

codes.name: Naming Rules Misapplied
codes.plain_name: Named the compound with the wrong rules
codes.student_help: Ionic: no prefixes, Roman numeral for multivalent metals. Molecular: prefixes.
codes.description: Applies the wrong IUPAC naming system (prefixes on ionic compounds, no Roman numeral for a multivalent metal, wrong -ide/-ate/-ite ending, wrong organic parent chain).
codes.example: Names FeCl₃ 'iron trichloride' or CO₂ 'carbon oxide'.

tell_apart.how: If the rule is right but the Roman numeral is wrong because the charge was misremembered, use FAC_ION_CHARGE_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: naming decision flowchart.

codes.name: Lewis Structure Error
codes.student_help: Count total valence electrons first, then check every atom has a full shell.
codes.description: Miscounts valence electrons, leaves an atom without an octet, drops lone pairs, or misses a needed double bond; VSEPR shape follows from the wrong structure.
codes.example: Draws CO₂ with single bonds and two lone pairs on carbon.

tell_apart.how: If only the number of valence electrons for an element is misremembered, use FAC_SCIENCE_FACT_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: electron-count checklist (total, bonds, lone pairs, octets).

codes.name: Equilibrium Expression Error
codes.plain_name: Set up K or the ICE table wrongly
codes.student_help: Products over reactants, coefficients as powers, and leave out solids and pure liquids.
codes.description: Builds K, Ksp or an ICE table wrongly: coefficients as multipliers instead of exponents, solids or water included, change row not in the mole ratio.
codes.example: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ writes K = [NH₃]/(3[H₂][N₂]).

tell_apart.how: If the student misunderstands what equilibrium is, use CON_STATIC_EQUILIBRIUM.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: ICE-table template with the stoichiometry row filled in.

codes.name: Energy Sign Error
codes.plain_name: Got the sign of the energy change wrong
codes.student_help: Exothermic: ΔH is negative and energy is a product. Endothermic: ΔH is positive.
codes.description: Knows whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic but writes ΔH with the wrong sign, adds Hess's law steps without flipping signs, or uses q = mcΔT with the wrong sign for the system.
codes.example: Reverses a Hess's law equation but keeps ΔH = −286 kJ.

tell_apart.how: If the student thinks bond breaking releases energy, use CON_BOND_ENERGY.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: sign-tracking checkpoints at each Hess's law step.

codes.name: Rearranging Error
codes.student_help: Rearrange with symbols first, then put the numbers in.
codes.description: Rearranges an equation incorrectly to isolate the unknown (divides instead of multiplies, moves a term without changing its sign, loses a square).
codes.example: Rearranges PV = nRT for T as T = nR/PV.

tell_apart.how: If the algebra is right and only a number is computed wrongly, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.
If the starting formula is wrong, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION; this code is for a right formula rearranged wrongly.

codes.remediation: Symbol-first rearranging drill with a check by substituting simple numbers.

codes.name: Stopped Before the End
codes.student_help: Read the question again when you think you are done: is your last line the thing it asked for?
codes.description: Correct work that stops before the requested quantity or form is reached.
codes.example: Asked for the mass of CO₂ produced, finds 0.25 mol CO₂ and stops.

tell_apart.how: If the student aimed at a different target from the start, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION; here they were heading to the right target and stopped.
If an intermediate value is boxed as if it were final, use TST_DISTRACTOR_TRAP; if the work simply ends, use this code.

codes.remediation: Completion checklist: target quantity, unit, form asked for.

codes.name: Arithmetic Slip
codes.student_help: The steps make sense, with a small calculation slip in the numbers.
codes.description: An isolated arithmetic error with a sound method.
codes.example: Computes 0.250 × 44.01 as 1.10 instead of 11.0.

tell_apart.how: If the formula was rearranged wrongly before any arithmetic, use PRC_REARRANGEMENT.
If the slip comes from how the number was keyed in (brackets, exponent, mode), use FAC_CALCULATOR_ENTRY.

codes.remediation: Five-item rapid micro-drill on the same operation.

codes.name: Copy Error
codes.student_help: A number or sign changed when copying from one line to the next.
codes.description: Miscopies a digit, sign or term from one of the student's own lines to the next.
codes.example: Writes 0.0350 mol on one line and 0.0530 mol on the next.

tell_apart.how: If the value was read wrongly from the question itself, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN; this code is for copying between the student's own lines.
If a value was calculated wrongly rather than copied, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Line-to-line check habit.

codes.name: Molar Mass Slip
codes.student_help: Add one atomic mass for every atom, including the ones in brackets.
codes.description: Calculates a molar mass wrongly: misses atoms in brackets or hydrates, reads the atomic number instead of the mass, adds a wrong mass.
codes.example: Uses 62.0 g/mol for Ca(NO₃)₂ by counting the nitrate only once.

tell_apart.how: If the student confuses moles of molecules with atoms, use CON_MOLE_MEANING.
If the right masses are added wrongly, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: molar mass table (element, count, mass, subtotal).

codes.name: Ion Charge Recall
codes.plain_name: Remembered an ion's charge or formula wrongly
codes.student_help: Check the ion table for charges and polyatomic formulas.
codes.description: Uses the wrong charge for an ion or the wrong formula for a polyatomic ion.
codes.example: Writes sulfate as SO₃²⁻ or aluminium as Al²⁺.

tell_apart.how: If the charges are right and the formula is built wrongly, use PRC_FORMULA_FROM_IONS.
If an ion table was provided, use TST_REFERENCE_SHEET_UNUSED.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: ion flash cards.

codes.name: Fact Recall Slip
codes.student_help: Check this fact in your notes; it is one to memorise.
codes.description: Misremembers a specific fact: which acids are strong, valence electrons for a group, a solubility rule, a functional group name.
codes.example: Lists HF as a strong acid.

tell_apart.how: If the misunderstanding is about what 'strong' means, use CON_STRONG_VS_CONCENTRATED.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: spaced-recall quiz on the fact list.

codes.name: Unit Conversion
codes.student_help: A unit conversion was off, like centimetres to metres.
codes.description: Converts units wrongly or mixes units in one calculation.
codes.example: Uses 25 °C instead of 298 K in PV = nRT.

tell_apart.how: Here the number is wrong because of a conversion; in COM_MISSING_UNITS the number is right but the unit is not written.
If the conversion factor is right and the multiplication goes wrong, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Dimensional conversion bridge: write the factor as a fraction that cancels the old unit.

codes.name: Rounding / Precision
codes.student_help: A number was rounded too early or to the wrong decimal place.
codes.description: Rounds too early, or breaks the precision the question asks for.
codes.example: Reports 0.12345 mol from data given to three significant figures.

tell_apart.how: If the digits themselves are wrong, not just how many are kept, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Precision rules card: count significant figures in the givens, keep guard digits, round once.

codes.name: Calculator Entry
codes.student_help: The calculator was set up or used wrong, like being in radians instead of degrees.
codes.description: Wrong calculator mode, missing brackets when keying, or misread display.
codes.example: Types 6.02 × 10^23 without brackets in a division and gets an answer off by a factor of 10⁴⁶.

tell_apart.how: Use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP for mental or written arithmetic; this code is for results that only make sense as a keying slip (for example an answer off by a power of ten).

codes.remediation: Calculator entry drill with the same expression typed three ways.

codes.name: Answered a Different Question
codes.student_help: The work solved for something slightly different from what the question asked.
codes.description: Gives a correct answer to a different target than the one asked.
codes.example: Asked for the mass of oxygen needed, gives the mass of water produced.

tell_apart.how: If the work was heading to the right target and stopped short, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.
If a whole labelled part (b) is missing, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prompt deconstruction box: circle the verb, underline the target.

codes.name: Missing Units
codes.student_help: The final answer is missing its units.
codes.description: Omits units on a measurement answer.
codes.example: Writes the concentration as 0.50 with no mol/L.

tell_apart.how: If the number is wrong because of a conversion, use FAC_UNIT_CONVERSION.

codes.remediation: Unit slot habit: draw a box after the answer for the unit.

codes.name: Chemical Notation Error
codes.plain_name: Wrote the chemical symbols or formula wrongly
codes.student_help: Capital letter starts each element; subscripts go low, charges go high, and states go in brackets.
codes.description: Correct chemistry in wrong notation: case of element symbols, subscripts written as coefficients, charges missing on ions, missing states, wrong arrow (→ vs ⇌).
codes.example: Writes CO (carbon monoxide) as Co, or Na+ as Na.

tell_apart.how: If the charge written is the wrong value, use FAC_ION_CHARGE_RECALL; this code is for a right value written wrongly or left out.
If subscripts were changed to balance, use PRC_BALANCING.

codes.remediation: Tier 4: notation checklist.

codes.name: Unsupported Answer
codes.student_help: The answer is there, but the reason the question asked for is missing.
codes.description: Gives an answer, claim or 'show that' conclusion without the reasoning or working the question requires.
codes.example: 'Which has the higher boiling point, H₂O or H₂S? H₂O.' with no mention of hydrogen bonding.

tell_apart.how: COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN is for missing calculation steps; this code is for a missing explanation in words.
If an explanation is there but uses loose words, use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Claim-evidence-reasoning frame.

codes.name: Work Not Shown
codes.student_help: Write the formula, then the numbers in it, then the answer.
codes.description: A calculation answer with no formula, substitution or steps where the question expects them, so the method cannot be checked or credited.
codes.example: Writes 'mass = 11.0 g' for a stoichiometry question with no steps.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is wrong and there is no work, it is likely a guess: use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS. Use this code when the answer is right or close and only the steps are missing.
For a missing explanation in words, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.

codes.remediation: GRASS layout model: Given, Required, Analysis, Solution, Statement.

codes.name: Missing Labels / Definitions
codes.student_help: A graph, diagram or variable is missing labels, so it is unclear what it shows.
codes.description: Leaves out axis labels, scales, diagram labels or the 'let x be ...' definition that the work needs.
codes.example: Draws a heating curve with no axis labels or units.

tell_apart.how: COM_MISSING_UNITS is for a final numerical answer; this code is for diagrams, graphs and tables.

codes.remediation: Graph checklist card.

codes.name: Imprecise Terms
codes.plain_name: Used an everyday word where a subject term was needed
codes.student_help: Use the exact subject word instead of an everyday one.
codes.description: The idea is right but is stated with everyday or loose words where a specific scientific term is needed, so the answer is ambiguous.
codes.example: 'The salt melts into the water' when the student means dissolves.

tell_apart.how: If no reasoning is given at all, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.
If the wrong word shows a wrong idea (the student really thinks sugar melts in water), use the matching concept (CON) code instead.

codes.remediation: Word wall with paired everyday and scientific terms.

codes.name: Observation vs Inference
codes.plain_name: Mixed up what you saw with what it means
codes.student_help: Observations are what you saw, heard or measured; put explanations in the analysis.
codes.description: In lab or data questions, reports an explanation as if it were observed, or lists observations where an analysis or conclusion is asked for. Includes conclusions that go beyond the data.
codes.example: Observation: 'hydrogen gas was produced.' (what was seen was bubbles).

tell_apart.how: STR_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN is about how the investigation is planned; this code is about how results are written up.

codes.remediation: Two-column observation / inference sort.

codes.name: Blank / Time Attrition
codes.student_help: This part was left blank.
codes.description: Leaves a question or part with no attempt, from time pressure or a frustration block.
codes.example: A whole question with no writing at all.

tell_apart.how: If any work was started, use TST_ABANDONED_WORK.
If other parts of the same question are answered, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prerequisite baseline probe on that topic.

codes.name: Skipped Part
codes.student_help: One part of the question was skipped while the others were answered.
codes.description: Answers some parts of a multi-part question and leaves another out, likely without noticing.
codes.example: Question asks for the limiting reagent and the mass of product; gives only the mass.

tell_apart.how: If the whole question is empty, use TST_BLANK.
If the student answered something else instead of what was asked, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION.

codes.remediation: Part checklist habit.

codes.name: Distractor Trap
codes.plain_name: Middle step taken as the answer
codes.student_help: A middle step was treated as the final answer.
codes.description: Takes an intermediate value or a tempting wrong option as the final answer.
codes.example: Boxes the moles of product as the final answer when the question asks for grams.

tell_apart.how: If the work just stops, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION; this code is for presenting the wrong value as final.
If there is no work behind the choice, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS.

codes.remediation: 'Is this what was asked?' stop sign.

codes.name: Abandoned Work
codes.student_help: A good start was stopped or crossed out before reaching an answer.
codes.description: Starts a valid approach, then stops or crosses it out partway with no answer.
codes.example: Starts an ICE table, fills the first row, then crosses it out and moves on.

tell_apart.how: If nothing was written, use TST_BLANK.
If the work reaches a result one step short of the target, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.

codes.remediation: First-step confidence warm-up, then the same problem.

codes.name: Unchecked Answer
codes.student_help: A quick check would show this answer cannot be right, like a negative length.
codes.description: Gives an answer a quick check would show is impossible or absurd, and does not notice.
codes.example: Reports a percentage yield of 340% without comment.

tell_apart.how: Code the slip that caused the answer as well when it is visible; this code records that the impossible result was not caught.

codes.remediation: Estimate-then-check habit.

codes.name: Misread Given
codes.student_help: A number or sign in the question was read wrong.
codes.description: Misreads a number, sign or symbol printed in the question.
codes.example: Question gives 0.250 L; student uses 250 L.

tell_apart.how: If the slip happens between the student's own lines, use FAC_COPY_ERROR.
If the value is read right but used in the wrong place, use STR_WRONG_SUBSTITUTION.

codes.remediation: Given-data check habit.

codes.name: Unworked Guess
codes.student_help: An answer was written with no working, and it is not right.
codes.description: Writes a wrong final answer with no working shown, suggesting a guess.
codes.example: Writes 'pH = 4' with no working for a weak-acid pH question; the answer is 2.9.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is right but the work is missing, use COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN.

codes.remediation: Show-one-step routine.

codes.name: Reference Sheet Not Used
codes.student_help: If a value or formula is on the data sheet or periodic table, look it up instead of remembering it.
codes.description: Gets a value, constant or formula wrong that was printed on the provided data sheet, formula sheet or periodic table.
codes.example: Uses 35 g/mol for chlorine when the provided periodic table says 35.45.

tell_apart.how: If the formula or value was NOT provided, use the matching recall (FAC) code.

codes.remediation: Reference-sheet scavenger hunt before the test.
